correctness.rationale: For each u in (0,1], H_u f(z)=[1-(1-u)z]^{-1}f(uz/[1-(1-u)z]); direct Möbius composition gives H_u H_v=H_uv. The H1 and Bergman-A1 preadjoint composition norms are O(u^{-1}), so the spectral radius of H_t on BMOA/Bloch is at most t^{-1}. For every 0<|w|<t^{-1}, s_k=(log w+2πik)/log t has Re s_k>-1, and independent H1 predual eigenvectors (1-z)^{s_k} and their J-images produce an infinite-dimensional adjoint eigenspace; the primal (w-H_t) range closure therefore has infinite codimension. Closedness of Fredholm essential spectrum yields the entire closed disk and, with the radius bound, equality for H_t. A local variable z=v/(1+v) shows each putative eigenfunction is a scalar z^k/(1-z)^{k+1}, not Bloch, so H_t has empty point spectrum. Strict convergence radius rho>t^{-1} ensures F(H_t)=Σa_jH_t^j converges and permits holomorphic spectral mapping in B(X) and the Calkin algebra. Factorization of F(z)-λ by finitely many zeros on a neighborhood of the compact disk leaves injective factors, proving F(H_t) has no eigenvalues even when distinct w share the same F-image. The same predual eigenspaces give infinite-codimensional range closures at all F(w), 0<|w|<t^{-1}. value.rationale: This is an all-parameter spectral and Fredholm-essential classification for natural discrete Hausdorff operators on two standard nonreflexive holomorphic function spaces. Infinite-codimensional residual obstruction throughout an analytic disk despite atomically supported positive measure distinguishes it sharply from generic boundary-Fredholm formulas; its exact spectral-image property is useful beyond the two-atom example. The exact hypothesis rho>t^{-1}, absence of point spectrum and failure of the prior sectorial assumption make this a motivated structural theorem, not an unmotivated coefficient calculation.
